inverse: Within admitted selection traces no non-English/non-Text row, later matching group or dated author above cutoff reaches normal PD output. not_pd selects the opposite date predicate. Fetch success excludes missing-log append for that attempt.

A JSONL row permits any catalog with the matching selected fields and first-match/PD/skip predicates; unselected rows and prior skip entries are ambiguous. Missing log only identifies unavailable attempt, not remote absence forever.
limitations: UTF-8 catalogs; exact header names and row width; u32 dates; bounded counters and filesystem availability. Malformed CSV is tolerated. Fetch paths/id safety and live HTTP remain unexecuted.
Partial syntax and bounded synthetic helper checks; no command/corpus/model/download effects, universal proof or percentage surrogate.
state: Selection keeps source row order and assigns at most one group per row. Header errors precede output creation, later write failures need not roll back. PD is an author-date heuristic, not legal certification. Existing skip entries match digit strings after the last pg occurrence.
